disease_label_per_paper: Catastrophic antiphospholipid syndrome treated with plasma exchange
presentation_summary: 52-year-old man with 12-year primary APS presented after recent acute bacterial prostatitis with deterioration, weight loss, splinter hemorrhages, leg ulcers, and livedo reticularis.
Initial evaluation showed ECG ST depression, LV dysfunction, troponin 16.3 ug/L, thrombocytopenia, high CRP, therapeutic-range INR elevation on anticoagulation, and microscopic hematuria.
Within days he developed platelet collapse, severe hypoxemic respiratory failure, massive right adrenal hemorrhage, and acute renal failure.
Daily plasma exchange was started on day 6 with rapid improvement in oxygenation, platelet count, troponin, and creatinine.

presenting_symptoms.source_text_value: deterioration of his general condition, with weight loss

risk_context.source_text_value: primary antiphospholipid syndrome for twelve years, with one episode of deep vein thrombosis, migraine, and persistent high titers of IgG anti-cardiolipin and anti-beta2GPI antibodies
three weeks before admission, acute bacterial prostatitis treated by ciprofloxacin for 2 weeks
prothrombin time within the therapeutic range (INR: 4.35)

observations.source_text_value: ECG ST-segment depression in the lateral territory and echocardiography showed LV dysfunction with EF 30-35%

course_observations.source_text_value: platelet count decreased to 16 x 10^3/mm3 on day 3
acute hypoxemic respiratory failure requiring high-flow nasal cannula oxygen therapy
CT scan showed massive right adrenal hemorrhage
acute renal failure with serum creatinine increased to 246 umol/L

imaging.source_text_value: left ventricular dysfunction with an ejection fraction between 30 and 35% but no regional wall motion abnormalities
diffuse defects but no arguments in favor of pulmonary embolism; severe hypoxemia

microbiology.result: recent acute bacterial prostatitis treated before admission
microbiology.source_text_value: acute bacterial prostatitis treated by ciprofloxacin for 2 weeks

serology.source_text_value: aCL IgG 76.7 GPL, IgM 17.4 MPL initially; later aCL IgG 147.7 GPL, IgM 81.4 MPL
anti-beta2GPI IgG 83.2 SGU, IgM 30.8 SMU initially; later IgG 124.8 SGU, IgM 148.2 SMU

confirmatory_findings.finding: Known primary APS with persistent high-titer aPL antibodies
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: primary antiphospholipid syndrome for twelve years with persistent high titers of IgG anti-cardiolipin and anti-beta2GPI antibodies
myocardial injury, thrombocytopenia, hypoxemic respiratory failure, adrenal hemorrhage, and acute renal failure developed within days

quality_warnings: aPL titers are stored in serology/confirmatory_findings, not ordinary observations.
No schistocytes were reported and this negative TMA-like evidence is retained.
DIC-like coagulation evidence is not invented; INR is retained as anticoagulation-confounded context.
